sheet_prompts.b:
Draw ONE image: the DAMAGE sprite sheet for Axeman.

The attached image is the APPROVED MASTER design of this unit. It is the sole authoritative reference.

ERA / VISUAL THEME: Early Copper / Bronze Age melee infantry (Era 1–2): clean hand-painted historical 2D strategy art matching the Warrior and Swordsman sprites.

WHAT TO DRAW:
DAMAGE (4 frames, a grid of 2 by 2): the master's standing pose four times, the unit progressively hurt. Keep the legs and
   feet EXACTLY where they are in the master in all four frames (the game builds the walk from each of these drawings); any
   slump shows only in the head, shoulders and arms. In every frame the two legs are separate posts with a visible gap of
   empty background between them from the boots up, both feet flat on one ground line; mud, bandages and torn cloth never
   join the legs. Keep any prop the unit holds a hand's width clear of the
   boots. Keep the same headgear in all four frames (frame 3 may dent it) and every prop whole in frames 1 to 3 (frame 4 may
   break it, still held). (1) healthy, identical to the master; (2) light: dirt on clothes and legs,
   one clear slash across the garment, a scuffed hem; (3) serious: torn garment and sleeve, a dented leather cap, a scuffed shield and a nicked bronze axe blade, a few dark-maroon
   stains, messy hair; (4) critical: bandages on chest and forearm, a bruised face, a split leather cap, a torn tunic, a cracked shield rim and a notched axe haft, still in his hands, a tired slumped
   head and shoulders. Each frame must look clearly worse than the one before at a glance.

MANDATORY RULES FOR THIS SHEET:
- Authoritative reference: match the attached master image EXACTLY (the same face, brown hair and short brown beard, bronze-rimmed leather cap, red tunic, leather belt with bronze buckle, bracers, dark wool trousers, brown leather boots, wooden-hafted bronze battle axe and round hide shield with bronze boss). Same art style, bold dark outline, flat cel shading, palette, lighting, proportions, headgear, face, and held items in every frame. Do not redesign anything.
- Strict side view facing RIGHT, identical scale across every frame. Do NOT zoom in on a crouching, kneeling, or fallen pose.
- Leave clear empty #FF00FF magenta space (at least 20% of a figure width) between every pair of neighbouring figures and around all four outer edges of the image. No figure touches another figure or the image border.
- Nothing detached from a figure: no floating arrows, bullets, sparks, dust clouds, debris, motion arcs, or disconnected smoke puffs. Every weapon, shield, flame, or smoke wisp stays physically connected to the figure.
- BACKGROUND: one completely flat, uniform solid pure magenta (#FF00FF) background filling the entire image behind the unit. NO transparency checkerboard, NO grey-and-white grid, NO gradient, NO drop shadow, NO ambient glow, NO vignette, NO soft semi-transparent edges. Every outline, smoke puff, flame, dust cloud, or effect must be 100% solid, opaque, and hard-edged with a clean dark ink outline against the #FF00FF magenta so nothing blends into purple. Put nothing magenta, pink, or purple anywhere on the unit.
- Paint his tunic saturated pure red (#E01010), exactly as in the master; it is the ONLY bright red anywhere in the image. Wounds, stains, rust, and fire are dark maroon, brown, grey, yellow-orange, or black — never bright red. Family-friendly, no blood and no gore.
- No text, labels, numbers, boxes, borders, grid lines, ground planes, or shadows.
- Do NOT draw a walk, run, gallop, rolling, or flying cycle; the game animates movement itself.
- CRITICAL FOR WALK RIGGING: keep every leg and foot/hoof in the EXACT position of the master with a clear solid #FF00FF magenta gap between every pair of legs in ALL 4 frames. Mud, bandages, weapons, or torn cloth must never bridge or touch across the leg gap.

REQUIRED CORRECTIONS FROM PREVIOUS ATTEMPT (fix every item):
- Owner review feedback: Helmet consistency: in frame 3 the leather cap has a ragged, spiky crown that does not match frame 4. Keep the SAME smooth rounded bronze-rimmed leather cap silhouette in all four frames; frame 3 may show only one small dent and a scuff, no torn or jagged top; frame 4 may add a single split along the same cap shape. Do not change the cap's shape, size or position between frames 3 and 4.
